findings: The company reports its "Kriti" platform serves as a cloud-based enterprise spatial data infrastructure enabling field mapping, asset inventory management, and spatial data logging.
The company reports its "Smartout" platform acts as an integrated geospatial analysis and outage intelligence GIS platform focused on location dynamics and business intelligence.
We verified that the company offers web, mobile, and cloud-based software platforms (Kriti and Smartout) targeting asset management and location analytics using open-source architecture.

findings: The company developed a statewide Lake Management and Monitoring System for the government's Mission Kakatiya project in Telangana, which processed 20 years of satellite imagery to map approximately 40,000 surface water bodies across an area of 100,000 square kilometers, according to the official Kaiinos Geospatial website.

The company reports executing a rooftop solar digital twin project for an enterprise client, mapping building attributes such as footprint, height, orientation, and shading for over 65,000 houses across 2 cities using surface models extracted from drone and satellite imagery, as detailed on the Kaiinos Geospatial capabilities platform.
The rating rests on verified, large-scale deployments involving decades of satellite historical records and combined drone imagery processing for state government and enterprise clients.

findings: The company partnered with the Telangana government and IIIT-Hyderabad to develop the open-source Lake Management and Monitoring System (LMMS) supporting Mission Kakatiya, utilizing optimized NDWI calculations and rule-based classification algorithms on multispectral satellite data, according to Open Source For You.
The company reports developing "Dharani," a machine learning platform built to automate the extraction of building footprints from satellite imagery, as stated by Industrial Automation India.
We verified that the company has integrated rule-based classification and machine learning algorithms into geospatial platforms deployed for regional government initiatives.

findings: The company reports that its GIS platform integrates directly with major enterprise systems of record including SCADA, IoT, ERP (SAP and Oracle), Maximo, ADMS, AMI head-end, and billing systems during its standard deployment workflows.

The company reports a technical preference and commercial strategy emphasizing compliance with Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) open interfaces and standards to ensure long-term data interoperability and prevent proprietary vendor lock-in.

The rating rests on the company's documented capacity to integrate its platform with legacy enterprise architectures like SAP and Oracle ERP systems, alongside its compliance with open OGC standard interfaces.

findings: The company reports developing machine learning and deep learning algorithms for satellite data processing, real-time IoT sensor queues, and three core platforms: Kriti (enterprise field logging), Smartout (location dynamics and outage intelligence), and Dharani (a machine learning system for building footprint extraction), according to its official website.

The company presented its geospatial research work at the National Symposium on "Innovations in Geospatial Technology for Sustainable Development" in Shillong, an industry event organized by the Indian Society of Geomatics and the North-Eastern Space Applications Centre, according to an official corporate announcement.
The rating rests on its clear focus on machine learning algorithms for automated spatial feature extraction and its origins out of the Lab for Spatial Informatics at IIIT-Hyderabad.
